model_interpretation.claim: Static scheduling of the outer row loop assigns disjoint, contiguous output rows with uniform work while preserving the existing r-c-k accumulation order. A per-call thread cap of min(max(threads, 1), 8, n) tests scaling without changing global OpenMP state. Matrices below 128 remain serial to avoid team-startup overhead; this cutoff is a hypothesis to measure, not a demonstrated speedup.

items.subject: OpenMP work partitioning and thread scaling
items.objective: Make OpenMP decomposition and scaling the primary question. First establish a controlled parallel speedup using the existing r-c-k dot-product traversal, with disjoint output ownership; compare sensible row or output-region partitions, scheduling, and thread counts up to min(threads, 8). Avoid overhead on small inputs when measurements justify it. After this anchor is measured, correctness-preserving kernel changes may be explored as explicit interactions; record whether a timing change came from scheduling, thread count, or kernel order. Validate all official sizes and record failed variants.
